rhythm.value: 31.54 s, 20 corrected shots (detector: 10 shots, 9 cuts), 19 picture changes: 9 hard cuts to a new scene (0.708, 1.625, 3.375, 11.125, 15.292, 17.792, 19.25, 21.667, 27.375), 4 reframes on the same interface (punch-in 6.583, punch-out 8.083, macro 9.667, lateral jump 16.625), 4 text swaps on a held ground (2.792, 4.417, 29.583, 30.5) and 2 dissolves (5.604, mid of F127-F142; 25.646, mid of F612-F619). Holds: 0.71, 0.92, 1.17, 0.58, 1.04, 1.19, 0.98, 1.50, 1.58, 1.46, 4.17, 1.33, 1.17, 1.46, 2.42, 3.98, 1.73, 2.21, 0.92, 1.04 s; median 1.26 s, 36 changes per minute. Two halves: before 15.29 s the median hold is 1.17 s (type and the first demo), after it 1.46 s (louder music, longer answer holds). The two longest holds (4.17 s and 3.98 s) are the two answers being generated: the film spends its time on proof. Clock: the music and the on-screen text; Whisper found no words. I cannot hear the film. Against the beat grid (123 BPM, tempo confidence 0.55, beat regularity 0.95, downbeat confidence 0.17, so no bar grid is claimed): all corrected changes 9/19 within 80 ms of a beat vs 0.33 chance (lift 1.4), quiet half 3/10 vs 0.32 (chance), loud half 6/9 vs 0.33 (lift 2.0, n = 9, weak; the 16.625 reframe is 163 ms before a beat), 1/19 within a frame of a downbeat vs 0.04; signed median cut-to-beat +0.024 s. Onsets run 3.8/s in the quiet half and 7.0/s in the loud half, so onset ratios (10/19 within 80 ms vs 0.73 chance) mean nothing. Loudness swells (50 ms RMS, local max over +-0.3 s, > 1.35x section median, cut within 0.1 s) sit near cuts at chance (quiet 4/10 vs 0.37, loud 1/9 vs 0.22). sync.json (detector cuts, full-frame re-analysis): cutsOnBeat 0.556 vs 0.33, lift 1.68; cutsOnOnset 0.333 vs 0.727; downbeat-frame 0 vs 0.044 (lift 0); signed median -0.025 s. Detector 9 cuts, corrected 19 changes (corrections below). Crop: the earlier analysis copy was falsely cropped to x 308-1278 by the static-bands detector; source.json crop is now null and every measured layer (shots, OCR, motion, sync) was re-run on the full 1280x720 frame. Only a grey watermark sits top left. OCR boxes at x=0 at 16.5-17.0 s and 20.0-21.5 s are real: the headline-size field runs off the left edge while the camera follows the caret.
evidence: audio.json tempo.beatsSec, downbeatsSec, onsetsSec, sections, silence

value.name: giant-word-pull-out
value.description: The first word fills and overflows the frame at F0 (glyph box at least 73% of frame width and 61% of height, cropped by both edges; OCR box 0.667 x 0.342 of frame at 0-0.5 s), then pulls back on expo.out: motion.json fits a pull-out of z -0.90 (about 2.5x) starting 0.03 s, 90% of travel in 0.43 s; the diff falls from 27 at F3-F4 to under 6 by F10, and the word is settled at 43% of frame width, centred, by F14 (0.58 s). It holds 2 frames and hard-cuts at F17. A soft blue light hangs at the left edge throughout.
value.why: Starting inside the word gives the eye a single shape and a direction (outward) before anything is read; the fast-out ease spends the motion in the first 6 frames, so the word is still for its last 7 frames and reads at once.

evidence: motion.json s001 camera: pull_out z -0.9015, t5Sec 0.068 to t95Sec 0.496, ease expo.out, cubicBezier [0.288, 0.264, 0.032, 1.108]

value.name: ui-punch-in-reframe
value.description: Four hard reframes on the same interface instead of a zoom: F158 (6.583) cuts from the wide panel to about 1.8x on the prompt field (prompt line OCR box height 0.037 wide -> 0.064-0.066 close; title 0.044 -> 0.064-0.080, clipped by the right edge) as typing starts; F194 (8.083) cuts back to wide when the typed question is longer than the close frame; F232 (9.667) cuts to a macro of the send button at about 7x; later, in the headline-size prompt, F399 (16.625) jumps sideways at the same scale to the field's right end so the send button and cursor are in frame. Holds 1.50 s, 1.58 s, 1.46 s, then 1.17 s. Each close shot drifts slowly (camera move right/push in) and none animates the scale.
value.why: The eye stays on the caret: the cut-in arrives as the first letter does, the cut-out as the line outgrows the frame, and the macro tells the viewer where the next action is. Cuts are cheaper than zooms on a white UI: nothing has to be blurred and the text is sharp on every frame.

value.name: accelerate-into-cut
value.description: Five outgoing shots end on a camera drift that accelerates right up to a hard cut, and the incoming shot continues the direction and decelerates. Send-button macro drifts up F262-F266 (diff 1.4 -> 3.7) into the chat where the sent bubble rises F267-F270; the table drifts left into 15.292 (motion.json s007 circ.in, 90% of travel 14.84-15.24 s, 0.40 s, ending 0.05 s before the cut); the clicked field drifts up F418-F426 (diff 0.8 -> 2.3) and the next card rises and settles F427-F433; the benefit card pans left F454-F461 (diff 2.5 -> 4.3) into 19.25; the typed field rises and blurs F509-F519 (diff 3.1 -> 5.1) into the chat at F520.
value.why: On a white-on-white interface a hard cut can read as a glitch; momentum carried across it reads as one camera, and the speed peaks exactly at the cut so the change hides in motion blur.

evidence: motion.json s007 camera.ease circ.in [0.5, 0.148, 0.754, 0.245], t5Sec 14.844 to t95Sec 15.242

value.name: skeleton-shimmer-to-content
value.description: The answer arrives as a purple-to-lilac vertical-band placeholder (#A453EC to #D1D6FD) that grows from a dot beside the reply line at F328 (about 1% of frame width) to the full table size by F340 (about 47% of width, 60% of height) while the chat scrolls up; its bands slide sideways as it grows (diff 2.3 rising to 8.2 at F336, falling to 3.0 by F350). The table's text dissolves in through the bands F344-F350 and the gradient fades to the table's pale header colour. 22 frames, 0.92 s. The detector read this as a whip (13.71-14.71); it is one shot.
value.why: The eye already sits on the reply line; the placeholder grows out of that point so the eye is carried to the table's top-left corner and is there when the text resolves. The shimmer stands for work without a spinner, and its size tells the viewer how much answer is coming.

value.name: silence-gap-before-drop
value.description: Once the table has resolved (F350, 14.58 s) the music falls to near silence: 50 ms RMS about 50 against a quiet-section median of 1322, from about 14.5 s; audio.json marks silence 14.75-15.21. RMS starts to climb at about 15.18 s, the picture hard-cuts to the new pale-blue ground at F367 (15.292), about 3 frames into the rise, and the level reaches the loud section (RMS about 9000 against a loud median of 5072) at about 15.55 s, 6 frames after the cut. Section energy 0.16 before, 0.48 after. Measured from the waveform; that this is a riser into a drop is inferred, as I cannot hear it.
value.why: The silence gives the proof room: for 0.7 s the only thing happening is the table on screen. Cutting inside the rise, ahead of the hit, makes the new ground feel like it causes the music to return.
